subject: c12-chem
scope: CBSE Class XII Chemistry (043) 2026–27 written/theory Board-exam preparation; practical/internal-assessment material excluded.

reference.label: Solutions — Tip 1
reference.text: Keep molarity and molality distinct; check whether temperature can affect the concentration expression.

reference.label: Solutions — Tip 2
reference.text: For colligative properties, identify the correct property and apply the van't Hoff factor when abnormal association or dissociation is involved.

reference.label: Solutions — Tip 3
reference.text: In numerical questions, write the known quantities and units before substituting.

reference.label: Solutions — Tip 4
reference.text: Check whether the question asks for molar mass, elevation/depression or osmotic pressure before choosing the relation.

reference.label: Solutions — Tip 5
reference.text: Link abnormal molar mass to association/dissociation rather than treating it as an unrelated exception.

reference.label: Electrochemistry — Tip 1
reference.text: Identify anode and cathode from oxidation and reduction rather than relying only on sign memory.

reference.label: Electrochemistry — Tip 2
reference.text: Write the overall cell reaction before constructing the Nernst reaction quotient.

reference.label: Electrochemistry — Tip 3
reference.text: Keep conductance, conductivity and molar conductivity distinct.

reference.label: Electrochemistry — Tip 4
reference.text: For electrolysis, track charge passed and electron stoichiometry carefully.

reference.label: Electrochemistry — Tip 5
reference.text: Connect batteries, fuel cells and corrosion to electrochemical-cell principles.

reference.label: Chemical Kinetics — Tip 1
reference.text: Identify the reaction order before choosing an integrated rate equation or half-life relation.

reference.label: Chemical Kinetics — Tip 2
reference.text: Keep rate units separate from rate-constant units.

reference.label: Chemical Kinetics — Tip 3
reference.text: For Arrhenius questions, identify the quantities being compared before substituting.

reference.label: Chemical Kinetics — Tip 4
reference.text: Use concentration data exactly as specified; do not mix initial and instantaneous values.

reference.label: Chemical Kinetics — Tip 5
reference.text: Connect collision theory with activation energy and temperature dependence.

reference.label: d- and f-Block Elements — Tip 1
reference.text: Revise periodic position and electronic configuration before transition-metal trends.

reference.label: d- and f-Block Elements — Tip 2
reference.text: Separate general transition-metal behaviour from specific exceptions and compounds.

reference.label: d- and f-Block Elements — Tip 3
reference.text: Learn important compounds with their preparation, properties and uses.

reference.label: d- and f-Block Elements — Tip 4
reference.text: Keep lanthanoids and actinoids distinct.

reference.label: d- and f-Block Elements — Tip 5
reference.text: Use a compact trend table for repeated revision.

reference.label: Coordination Compounds — Tip 1
reference.text: Identify central metal, ligands, coordination number and oxidation state before naming a complex.

reference.label: Coordination Compounds — Tip 2
reference.text: Apply nomenclature systematically.

reference.label: Coordination Compounds — Tip 3
reference.text: Classify the relevant types of isomerism from the actual structure.

reference.label: Coordination Compounds — Tip 4
reference.text: Use Werner's theory and bonding concepts to explain geometry and coordination number.

reference.label: Coordination Compounds — Tip 5
reference.text: Check the overall complex charge before calculating oxidation state.

reference.label: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes — Tip 1
reference.text: Identify the substrate class and C–X bond before choosing a reaction.

reference.label: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes — Tip 2
reference.text: Keep substitution and elimination reactions distinct.

reference.label: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes — Tip 3
reference.text: Remember that haloarenes do not behave exactly like haloalkanes.

reference.label: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes — Tip 4
reference.text: Write reagents and conditions along with reactions.

reference.label: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes — Tip 5
reference.text: Revise polyhalogen compounds with their prescribed uses.

reference.label: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers — Tip 1
reference.text: Classify the alcohol, phenol or ether before predicting its reaction.

reference.label: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers — Tip 2
reference.text: Distinguish reactions of alcohols from reactions of phenols.

reference.label: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers — Tip 3
reference.text: Track oxidation products carefully for primary and secondary alcohols.

reference.label: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers — Tip 4
reference.text: Learn commercially important alcohols with their uses.

reference.label: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers — Tip 5
reference.text: For ethers, identify the groups and conditions before predicting cleavage products.

reference.label: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids — Tip 1
reference.text: Identify aldehyde, ketone or carboxylic acid before selecting a reaction.

reference.label: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids — Tip 2
reference.text: Organise carbonyl reactions by reagent and product.

reference.label: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids — Tip 3
reference.text: Check oxidation/reduction conditions carefully.

reference.label: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids — Tip 4
reference.text: Use structural formulas when distinguishing similar carbonyl compounds.

reference.label: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids — Tip 5
reference.text: Connect carboxylic-acid acidity, preparation, reactions and uses.

reference.label: Amines — Tip 1
reference.text: Classify the amine before discussing basicity or chemical behaviour.

reference.label: Amines — Tip 2
reference.text: Keep basicity trends separate from nucleophilic reactions.

reference.label: Amines — Tip 3
reference.text: Learn diazotisation and coupling as a connected sequence.

reference.label: Amines — Tip 4
reference.text: Track the aromatic ring and diazonium group carefully.

reference.label: Amines — Tip 5
reference.text: Use reaction maps for synthesis involving diazonium salts.

reference.label: Biomolecules — Tip 1
reference.text: Organise carbohydrates by type, monomer and examples.

reference.label: Biomolecules — Tip 2
reference.text: Connect proteins with amino acids, peptide linkage and function.

reference.label: Biomolecules — Tip 3
reference.text: Learn enzymes through their catalytic role.

reference.label: Biomolecules — Tip 4
reference.text: Use a compact table for vitamins and prescribed functions.

reference.label: Biomolecules — Tip 5
reference.text: Distinguish nucleic acids and hormones by structure and function.

mistakes: Applying colligative-property relations without checking the van't Hoff factor.
Using the Nernst equation with an incorrect reaction quotient.
Mixing zero-order and first-order equations/half-life relations.
Confusing rate-constant units with reaction-rate units.
Memorising trends without distinguishing exceptions and compounds.
Losing track of ligand names, coordination number, oxidation state, geometry or isomerism.
Writing organic reactions without checking reagent, condition, substrate class and major product.
Confusing amine basicity trends or mixing diazotisation and coupling conditions.
Memorising classifications without connecting monomers, linkages, functions and examples.
order: Do Solutions, Electrochemistry and Chemical Kinetics first; practise their numerical patterns immediately after learning each concept.
Study d- and f-Block with a compact trend/compound sheet and revise it repeatedly rather than cramming once.
Complete Coordination Compounds next, especially terminology, nomenclature, isomerism and bonding.
Study the organic sequence in order: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes → Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers → Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids → Amines.
Finish Biomolecules with linked tables for carbohydrates, proteins, enzymes, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones.
After the first complete pass, practise mixed conversion/reaction questions and numerical questions together.
Use the official sample paper and marking scheme to check answer style and coverage.
